metadata.title: 如何进入 Google AI Overviews（AIO）

text:
# 如何进入 Google AI Overviews（AIO）

- 作者：Flavio Amiel（@fba）
- 原帖发布时间：2026-07-22 16:11（北京时间）
- 原帖：https://x.com/fba/status/2079841834625331658
- 收藏日期：2026-10-29
- 英文标题：How to Rank in Google's AI Overviews (AIO)

## 中文全文

你无法像在搜索结果中排名第 1 那样，在 AI Overview 中取得“排名”——它没有一套独立的 AIO 排名系统。Google 使用检索增强生成，从常规搜索索引中构建 AI Overviews。因此，一个页面需要先被收录、符合展示摘要的条件，并选择参与，才具备入选资格；当它成为某个子查询最清晰、最可信的信息来源时，就会被引用。

核心要点

- 不存在独立的“AIO 算法”。AI Overviews 通过[检索增强生成，也就是依据约束（grounding）](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide)，从 Google 的核心搜索索引中获取内容。
- 要具备资格，需要满足 3 个条件：页面被收录、有资格连同摘要一起展示，并且没有在 Search Console 中选择退出 AI 功能。
- Google 明确表示，不需要特殊标记、llms.txt 或“内容分块”——同样的 SEO 基本原则依然适用。
- 经过同行评审的研究（[GEO，KDD 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735)）发现，注明来源、加入引言和统计数据，最多可以让某个来源在 AI 回答中的可见度提高 40%；堆砌关键词则没有这种作用。
- 被引用不等于获得点击。[Pew 发现](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/)，用户大约只会在 1% 的访问中点击 AI 摘要内部的链接。因此，既要争取引用，也要让品牌从中获益。

几乎每一篇“如何在 AI Overviews 中排名”的指南，从第一句话开始就把问题的框架设错了。不存在 AIO 排行榜，没有 AIO 排名因素，也没有一个按钮能把你放进那个展示框。Google 对此说得格外直接：[针对它的生成式 AI 功能做优化，就是针对搜索做优化](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide)——使用相同的索引、相同的质量系统、相同的基本原则。真正值得研究的问题不是“我怎样获得排名”，而是“什么会让 Google 的模型选择我的页面，作为它构建答案依据的来源之一”。

本指南会回答这个问题，然后介绍能够带来实际效果的 8 个步骤，最后说明一个任何 AIO 优化者都不能忽视的陷阱。

## 在 AI Overviews 中“排名”究竟意味着什么

AI Overview 是生成出来的，不是直接检索出来的。当你触发一个 AI Overview 时，Google 会运行两种值得理解的机制。第一种是[检索增强生成（RAG）](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide)，Google 也称其为 grounding，即依据约束：核心排名系统从索引中取出相关且新鲜的页面，模型对这些具体页面进行总结，同时展示可以点回原页面的链接。第二种是查询扇出（query fan-out）：模型不会只回答你的单个查询，而是围绕不同子主题发起一组相关搜索，并为每个搜索获取来源。Google 自己给出的例子是：搜索“如何修复长满杂草的草坪”时，背后会悄悄扇出成“最好的草坪除草剂”“不用化学药剂清除杂草”和“如何预防杂草”等查询。

这会直接带来两个结果。第一：你的页面可能因为一个你从未明确针对的子问题而被引用。第二：可见度的单位是段落，而不是页面——模型会为每个扇出查询提取最清晰、最容易抽取的答案。这改变了整项工作的思路。你不是在争夺一个蓝色链接，而是在为一组相关问题提供最佳答案，并把答案写成模型无需修改就能引用的形式。

这不是一个只值得少数人关注的小众功能。截至 2026 年年中，Google 表示，[AI Overviews 的月度用户超过 25 亿，AI Mode 超过 10 亿](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/new-controls-website-owners/)。

## 第 1 步——确认你确实具备资格

在进行任何“优化”之前，先通过准入门槛。要出现在 AI Overviews 或 AI Mode 中，页面必须被收录、符合在搜索结果中连同摘要一起展示的条件，而且网站必须[在 Search Console 中参与搜索的生成式 AI 功能](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide)，也就是没有选择退出。如果你禁止摘要（`nosnippet`、`max-snippet:0`），就相当于退出了被引用。检查 Search Console 中的生成式 AI 效果报告，确认你是否已经出现，以及出现的是哪些页面、涉及哪些国家。

## 第 2 步——拿下基础查询，包括扇出的子查询

由于 AIO 以索引中的内容为依据，那些已经在目标查询及其子问题上排名良好的页面，就是候选来源。因此，第一个着力点很常规：取得排名。但还要再深入一层——梳理查询扇出。针对一个目标主题，列出模型可能发起的子问题，包括比较类、“最佳”类、“如何做”类、“对比”类、定义类和疑虑类查询，并确保你要么在每个问题上取得排名，要么在页面中设置回答它的章节。你要建立的是对一组问题的覆盖，而不是对一个关键词的覆盖。

## 第 3 步——在开头 40—60 词内给出能够独立成立的答案

模型引用的是段落，而且更偏好能够独立成立的答案。每个页面以及每个主要章节的开头，都应给出直接、可提取的回答：即使完全脱离上下文、单独复制粘贴，也仍然说得通。不要写“正如上文所见”，也不要使用指向别处内容的代词。可作参考的是：[Pew 的数据中，AI 摘要长度的中位数为 67 词](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/)。如果你的答案需要用整页内容铺垫才能让人理解，它就不适合被引用。本文开头的引用段落就是一种示范。

## 第 4 步——发布非同质化的第一手内容

Google 表示，这一条对你在 AI 搜索中出现的影响，[“比它给出的任何其他建议都更大”](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide)。模型会阅读许多来源；一个页面如果只是复述网上已有的内容，就没有为综合生成答案增加任何东西。Google 自己举出的对比很鲜明：“首次购房者的 7 条建议”属于同质化、可由模型生成的内容；而“我们为什么放弃房屋检查并省了钱：看看下水管道内部”则是具体、第一手的视角，模型无法自行创造。如果模型本来就能写出你的页面，它便不需要引用它。

## 第 5 步——加入生成式引擎偏好的证据：统计数据、来源和引言

在这里，独立研究与 Google 所说的“做好 SEO 就行”形成了有价值的差别。[发表于 KDD 的 GEO 研究](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735)在数千个查询上测试了不同的内容干预方法，发现添加引用来源、来自可信来源的引言和统计数据，会显著提高某个来源在生成式答案中被引用的频率，可见度最多提升 40%；传统的关键词堆砌则毫无作用。同一研究方向后续的受控实验发现，明确的数字和近期日期有帮助，而单纯的格式美化作用较弱。这不是某种技巧，而是因为包含可验证、可引用证据的页面，在结构上更方便模型作为依据。效果因领域而异，因此要测试，不要想当然。

## 第 6 步——建立信任基础：署名作者、审核、日期和一手引用

本文带有审核说明、可见的更新日期和来源链接，原因与 Investopedia 经常被引用一样：这些信号让页面不只是可读，而是值得引用。相较于匿名且没有日期的帖子，一个由具备资质的真实作者署名、标注日期、引用一手来源的页面，更适合让模型把答案归因于它。索引数据里也有一个迹象：[Pew 发现，政府来源在 AI 摘要中出现的比例，是标准搜索结果中的 3 倍，分别为 6% 和 2%](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/)。这从侧面反映了 AIO 对高可信来源的依赖程度。你不会变成一个 .gov 网站，但可以采取同样的做法：真实的人、真实的引用、真实的日期。

## 第 7 步——完整覆盖主题，并为每个术语建立内部链接

查询扇出会奖励覆盖广度。如果你的网站回答了整个问题群——定义、比较、操作方法和边缘情况——那么在同一个概览提取来源的多个子查询中，你就有更多机会进入候选范围。把正文中的每个专业术语链接到解释它的页面；这种正文内部链接，能够让爬虫和模型都理解一个主题，而且写作时顺手就能完成，不需要额外成本。这样，主题权威性就能同时服务于传统搜索和 AIO。

## 第 8 步——在 Search Console 中衡量表现，并在没有点击时获取品牌价值

使用 [Search Console 的生成式 AI 效果报告](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide)追踪出现情况，而不是使用那些声称掌握 Google“内部”指标的第三方工具——没有任何这类工具能够访问 Google 的排名或 AI 系统。然后，为下面这个难点做好准备。

## 人们对 AIO 的误解

无效的努力几乎总是用在了错误的层面上。追着 llms.txt 文件跑、把文案“分块”成碎片，或者“为了 AI”硬加 Schema，对 Google 的 AI 功能都没有帮助——[Google 对此说得很明确](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide)，因为它的系统会忽略那些文件，而且完全能够理解涵盖多个主题的页面。真正的陷阱，是只凭引用来衡量成败。[Pew 的浏览数据](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/)发现，在带有 AI 摘要的搜索中，用户仅有 8% 的情况会点击任何链接；没有 AI 摘要时，这一比例为 15%；而点击摘要内部链接的情况约为 1%。被引用能带来可见度和品牌印象，却很少带来访问。因此，先争取引用，再让引用本身发挥作用：使用不会被混淆的品牌名称，提出值得记住的观点，并建立一个不依赖那次很可能不会发生的点击的自有渠道，例如邮件通讯或产品。

## AIO、传统 SEO 与 GEO 的对比

传统 SEO——目标：让一个链接获得排名。单位：页面。着力点：相关性与权威性。回报：点击。通过排名和点击衡量。

AI Overviews（AIO）——目标：成为答案依据的引用来源。单位：段落或子查询。着力点：索引资格，以及有证据支持、便于引用的答案。回报：可见度，点击很少。通过 GenAI 效果报告衡量。

GEO，广义而言——目标：在不同 AI 引擎中被引用。单位：段落。着力点：证据、引用和统计数据。回报：提及与影响力。通过不同引擎中的引用份额衡量。

Google 自己的立场是：“AEO”和“GEO”描述的是 AI 搜索中的可见度，但在它看来，[这项工作仍然是 SEO](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide)——使用同样的索引和系统。

## 常见问题

**针对 AI Overviews，有什么特殊的优化方法吗？** 没有。[Google 表示](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features)，要出现在 AI Overviews 或 AI Mode 中，并没有额外要求或特殊优化方法；相同的 SEO 基本原则仍然适用，因为这些功能运行在核心搜索索引之上。

**我需要 llms.txt、Schema，或者把内容“分块”吗？** 不需要。[Google 搜索会忽略 llms.txt](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide)，不要求分块，也不需要为 AI 功能使用特殊 Schema。结构化数据仍然能帮助你获得传统富媒体搜索结果的展示资格，所以应该保留——只是不要把目的说成“为了 AI”。

**我能阻止 AI Overviews 使用我的内容吗？** 可以——[Search Console 提供了一个开关](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/new-controls-website-owners/)，允许你退出为生成式 AI 功能提供答案依据。不过，退出的网站不会从这些功能中获得流量或展示，而且该选择不会被用于其他场景的排名信号。

**出现在 AI Overview 中，真的能带来流量吗？** 很少通过直接点击带来流量。[Pew 的数据](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/)发现，在访问带有 AI 摘要的页面时，只有约 1% 的访问包含点击摘要内部链接的行为。应把 AIO 视为可见度和品牌渠道，而不是流量水龙头。

**哪些查询更容易触发 AI Overviews？** 较长、使用自然语言、以问题形式表达的查询，远比短查询更容易触发。[Pew 的数据](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/)显示，10 词以上的搜索中，有 53% 会出现摘要；只有 1 或 2 个词的搜索中，这一比例为 8%；全部搜索中约有 18% 会触发摘要。

## 最后的结论

你不是在 AI Overview 中取得排名，而是被它选中。先通过资格门槛：被收录、符合摘要展示条件、选择参与；然后在内容开头给出便于引用的答案，覆盖扇出的子查询；再向模型提供证据充分、由真实作者署名、由一手来源支持的第一手内容——独立研究表明，这些因素能够提高引用率，Google 自己也把它们视为质量的定义。接着，考虑到点击通常不会发生，就要在引用中建立品牌和自己的受众。做好这些，“在 AIO 中排名”就不再是一个神秘黑箱，而会回到它一直以来的本质：针对某个问题，成为互联网上最清晰、最可信的信息来源。

迷你术语表——AIO：AI 概览（AI Overviews）· RAG：检索增强生成，亦即依据约束（grounding）· GEO：生成式引擎优化 · AEO：答案引擎优化 · E-E-A-T：经验、专业性、权威性、可信度 · CTR：点击率 · MAU：月活跃用户 · PAA：其他用户还问了什么（People Also Ask）· SGE：搜索生成式体验。

来源

2. Google Search Central：《AI 功能与您的网站》。[原文](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features)。
3. Google：《为网站所有者带来新的机会、控制方式和洞察》。[原文](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/new-controls-website-owners/)，2026 年 6 月 3 日。
4. Aggarwal 等：《GEO：生成式引擎优化》，arXiv:2311.09735，KDD 2024。[论文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735)。

---

## 英文原文

You can't "rank" in an AI Overview the way you rank #1 in Search — there is no separate AIO ranking system. Google builds AI Overviews from its normal Search index using retrieval-augmented generation, so a page becomes eligible by being indexed, snippet-eligible, and opted in, then gets cited when it's the clearest, most trustworthy source for a sub-query.

Key takeaways

- There is no separate "AIO algorithm." AI Overviews pull from Google's core Search index via [retrieval-augmented generation (grounding)](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide).
- To be eligible you need three things: the page indexed, eligible to show with a snippet, and not opted out of AI features in Search Console.
- Google states plainly that no special markup, llms.txt, or "chunking" is required — the same SEO fundamentals apply.
- Peer-reviewed research ([GEO, KDD 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735)) found citing sources, adding quotations, and adding statistics can lift a source's visibility in AI answers by up to 40% — keyword stuffing does not.
- Being cited is not the same as getting a click. [Pew found](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/) users click a link inside an AI summary in roughly 1% of visits — so optimize for the citation and for brand capture.

Almost every "how to rank in AI Overviews" guide gets the framing wrong on the first line. There is no AIO leaderboard, no AIO ranking factor, and no button that puts you in the box. Google has been unusually direct about this: [optimizing for its generative AI features is optimizing for Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) — same index, same quality systems, same fundamentals. The interesting question is not "how do I rank," it's "what makes Google's model choose my page as one of the sources it grounds the answer in."

This guide answers that, then walks the 8 steps that move the needle — and ends with the trap nobody optimizing for AIO can afford to ignore.

## What "ranking" in AI Overviews actually means

An AI Overview is generated, not retrieved. When you trigger one, Google runs two mechanisms worth understanding. The first is [retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide), which Google also calls grounding: its core ranking systems fetch relevant, fresh pages from the index, and the model summarizes those specific pages while showing clickable links back to them. The second is query fan-out: instead of answering your one query, the model issues a set of related searches across sub-topics and pulls sources for each. Google's own example: a search for how to fix a weed-filled lawn quietly fans out into "best herbicides for lawns," "remove weeds without chemicals," and "how to prevent weeds."

Two consequences follow directly. One: your page can be cited for a sub-question you never explicitly targeted. Two: the unit of visibility is the passage, not the page — the model lifts the cleanest extractable answer to each fan-out query. That reframes the whole job. You're not fighting for one blue link; you're trying to own the best answer to a cluster of related questions, in a form a model can quote without editing.

This is not a niche feature to chase. As of mid-2026 Google reports [AI Overviews has over 2.5 billion monthly users and AI Mode over 1 billion](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/new-controls-website-owners/).

## Step 1 — Confirm you're actually eligible

Before any "optimization," clear the gate. To appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode a page must be indexed, eligible to be shown in Search with a snippet, and the site must be [included in Search's generative AI features in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) — i.e. not opted out. If you block snippets (nosnippet, max-snippet:0) you have opted out of being quoted. Check the Generative AI performance report in Search Console to confirm you're already appearing and for which pages and countries.

## Step 2 — Win the underlying queries, including the fan-out

Because AIO grounds on the index, pages that already rank well for the query and its sub-questions are the candidate pool. So the first lever is ordinary: earn the rankings. But go one level deeper — map the fan-out. For a target topic, list the sub-questions a model would fire (comparisons, "best," "how to," "vs," definitional, and objection queries) and make sure you either rank for each or have an on-page section that answers it. You're building coverage for a question cluster, not a keyword.

## Step 3 — Put a self-contained answer in the first 40–60 words

The model quotes passages, and it favors answers that stand alone. Lead each page (and each major section) with a direct, extractable answer that survives being copy-pasted with zero surrounding context — no "as we saw above," no pronouns pointing elsewhere. For calibration: in [Pew's data the median AI summary was 67 words long](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/). If your answer needs a whole page of build-up to make sense, it isn't quotable. The quote block at the top of this article is the pattern.

## Step 4 — Publish non-commodity, first-hand content

This is the one Google says will influence your presence in AI search ["more than any of the other suggestions"](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) it gives. The model reads many sources; a page that merely restates what's already online adds nothing to synthesize. Google's own contrast is sharp: "7 Tips for First-Time Homebuyers" (commodity, generatable) versus "Why We Waived the Inspection & Saved Money: A Look Inside the Sewer Line" (a specific, first-hand take a model can't produce on its own). If a model could have written your page, it won't need to cite it.

## Step 5 — Add the evidence generative engines prefer: statistics, sources, quotations

Here's where the independent research diverges usefully from Google's "just do good SEO." The [KDD-published GEO study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735) tested content interventions across thousands of queries and found that adding cited sources, quotations from credible sources, and statistics measurably raised how often a source was cited in generative answers — up to a 40% visibility gain — while old-school keyword stuffing did nothing. Later controlled work in the same line found explicit numbers and recent dates help, while cosmetic formatting alone is weak. The takeaway isn't a hack — it's that pages carrying verifiable, quotable evidence are structurally easier for a model to lean on. Effects vary by domain, so test rather than assume.

## Step 6 — Build the trust layer: named authors, review, dates, primary citations

The reason this article carries a review line, a visible update date, and linked sources is the same reason Investopedia gets cited: those signals make a page quotable rather than merely readable. A dated page from a named, credentialed author who cites primary sources is a safer thing for a model to attribute an answer to than an anonymous, undated post. There's an indexing tell here too — [Pew found government sources appeared in AI summaries three times as often as in standard results (6% vs 2%)](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/), a proxy for how much AIO leans on high-trust origins. You won't become a .gov, but you can adopt the same posture: real people, real citations, real dates.

## Step 7 — Cover the topic completely and interlink every term

Query fan-out rewards breadth. If your site answers the whole cluster — the definition, the comparison, the how-to, the edge cases — you become a candidate for more of the sub-queries a single overview pulls from. Link every jargon term in your body to the page that defines it; that in-body interlinking is what makes a topic legible to crawlers and models alike, and it's free at write time. This is topical authority doing double duty for classic Search and AIO.

## Step 8 — Measure in Search Console, and capture the brand when there's no click

Track appearances in the [Search Console Generative AI performance report](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide), not a third-party tool claiming "internal" Google metrics — none have access to Google's ranking or AI systems. Then plan for the hard part below.

## The thing people get wrong about AIO

The wasted effort is nearly always on the wrong layer. Chasing llms.txt files, "chunking" copy into fragments, or bolting on schema "for AI" does nothing for Google's AI features — [Google says so outright](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide), because its systems ignore those files and understand multi-topic pages fine. The real trap is measuring success by citation alone. [Pew's browsing data](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/) found people clicked any link on just 8% of searches with an AI summary versus 15% without, and clicked a link inside the summary about 1% of the time. Being cited buys you visibility and brand impression, rarely a visit. So win the citation — then make the citation itself do work: an unmistakable brand name, a claim worth remembering, and an owned channel (newsletter, product) that doesn't depend on the click that isn't coming.

## AIO vs. traditional SEO vs. GEO

Traditional SEO — goal: rank a link. Unit: the page. Lever: relevance and authority. Payoff: the click. Measured in rankings and clicks.

AI Overviews (AIO) — goal: be cited as a grounding source. Unit: the passage or sub-query. Lever: index eligibility plus quotable, evidenced answers. Payoff: visibility (a click is rare). Measured in the GenAI performance report.

GEO (broad) — goal: be cited across AI engines. Unit: the passage. Lever: evidence, citations, statistics. Payoff: mention and influence. Measured in citation share across engines.

Google's own position: "AEO" and "GEO" describe visibility in AI search, but from its perspective [that work is still SEO](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) — same index, same systems.

## Frequently asked questions

Is there a special way to optimize for AI Overviews? No. [Google states](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) there are no additional requirements or special optimizations to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode; the same SEO fundamentals apply because these features run on the core Search index.

Do I need llms.txt, schema, or to "chunk" my content? No. [Google ignores llms.txt for Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide), doesn't require chunking, and doesn't need special schema for AI features. Structured data still helps you qualify for classic rich results, so keep it — just not "for AI."

Can I stop AI Overviews from using my content? Yes — [Search Console has a toggle](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/new-controls-website-owners/) to opt out of grounding generative AI features, but opted-out sites receive no traffic or impressions from those features, and it isn't used as a ranking signal elsewhere.

Does appearing in an AI Overview actually bring traffic? Rarely as a direct click. [Pew's data](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/) found only about 1% of visits to pages with an AI summary involved clicking a link inside it. Treat AIO as a visibility and brand channel, not a traffic faucet.

What kinds of queries trigger AI Overviews? Longer, natural-language and question-style queries far more than short ones. In [Pew's data](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/), 53% of 10+ word searches produced a summary versus 8% of one- or two-word searches, and roughly 18% of all searches triggered one.

## The bottom line

You don't rank in an AI Overview; you get selected by it. Clear the eligibility gate (indexed, snippet-eligible, opted in), own the fan-out of sub-queries with quotable answers up top, and give the model evidence-rich, first-hand content signed by real people and backed by primary sources — the things independent research shows lift citation and Google itself says define quality. Then, because the click usually won't come, build the brand and the owned audience inside the citation. Do all that and "ranking in AIO" stops being a mystery box and becomes what it always was: being the clearest, most trustworthy source on the internet for the question.
